title: Replace Playwright camera-config scripts with typed reolink-cli wrapper (full subcommand coverage)
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-21, after 6/6 cameras alarm-delay fix in single session)
plan_section: V2-065. New structural integration: swap the stale `scripts/tune_510a_motion_sensitivity.py` Playwright path for a typed wrapper around the official Reolink CLI (`reolink/reolink-cli` GitHub). Operator verified the CLI today: applied stay-time=2 across 6 cameras in ~10 minutes with zero UI scraping and zero selector drift.
trigger: Operator 2026-09-21 ~10:50 EDT verbatim: 'I think it's time to go find the Reolink camera MCP on GitHub and see if you can use that to make the change'. Followed by ~11:30 EDT: 'Is there a way we can incorporate this into the farm surveillance V2 application instead of whatever other scripts we have for doing cameras?' And: 'I want it for the scope of all the camera commands and I just wanted as a function that we call manually when needed'.
background: Camera-config touchpoints in v1/parent repo rely on `scripts/tune_510a_motion_sensitivity.py` (Playwright + `cam_browser.py` line 228-252 `cb.gear()` selector). The selector drifted (firmware updates or selector never had the upper-LEFT-quadrant click trick from `cameras/RLC-510A.md` section 2.1 baked in). Dry-run `--read` on 192.168.1.73 failed 3/3 today: 'Gear panel did not open after 3 attempts'. The script also has a hardcoded recipe at lines 85-95 with no CLI override (Phase 6B.59 2026-08-02 set `delay_vehicle 0->2` deliberately, `delay_person` left at 0 with no rationale, became the root cause of today's Front Door Outside bbox-crop mismatch). Today's pivot to `reolink-cli 0.19.0` (Baichuan v20/v30 protocol, same as the camera web UI uses) verified: 12 writes + 12 reads, all 6 cameras at stay-time=2 for person/vehicle/dog_cat. Total time: ~10 minutes. Wrapper codifies that workflow so the next person doesn't re-discover it.

operator_guarantees.manual_only: No listener boot-time enforcement. `apply_recipe()` is callable on demand. Operator invokes explicitly when needed.
operator_guarantees.all_subcommands: Wrapper exposes the full reolink-cli surface (detect ai/motion, encode, audio, light, image, privacy, ptz, users, osd, record, events, vod, snapshot, preview, log, system, etc.) — not just alarm-delay.
operator_guarantees.alias_based: Per-call credential boilerplate (`REOLINK_USER=$X REOLINK_PASSWORD=***`) replaced by `reolink-cli device add` aliases (`--camera back`). Source of truth becomes `~/.local/share/reolink-cli/aliases.toml` (canonical store) + per-camera HTTP_USER/HTTP_PASS from `camera-creds.env` injected at registration time only.
operator_guarantees.no_playwright_in_v2: v2 repo never imports Playwright. Playwright path stays in v1/parent repo until archived.
operator_guarantees.env_tunable: Per AGENTS.md Step 3 all-knobs-env-tunable rule. Wrapper respects existing `FARM_REOLINK_CLI_BIN`, `FARM_REOLINK_GATEWAY_ADDR`, `FARM_CAMERA_CREDS_FILE` overrides (defaults baked in but overridable).
operator_guarantees.no_listener_restart: Wrapper does not boot the listener or restart it. Caller controls lifecycle.

shipping_definition: (a) `infra/reolink.py` exists with typed `ReolinkClient` class exposing per-subcommand methods returning dataclasses; (b) all 6 cameras registered as reolink-cli aliases (`device add`) using HTTP creds from `camera-creds.env`; (c) `config/camera_recipes.toml` is the canonical declarative recipe file (per-camera, per-subcommand); (d) `apply_recipe()` + `verify_recipe()` round-trip works end-to-end against the live fleet (no dry-run, no manual clicking); (e) `tests/test_reolink.py` covers all wrapper methods against a mock CLI (no real hardware); (f) `scripts/tune_510a_motion_sensitivity.py` is archived (not deleted, per AGENTS.md 'no deletions' rule); (g) `reolink-camera-config` skill in `~/.hermes/skills/local-ai/` updated to point at the new wrapper; (h) `bin/preflight_v2_only.sh` passes; (i) `ruff check .` reports zero new errors; (j) no listener restart needed (wrapper is not wired into listener boot).
scope_exclusions: No listener boot-time enforcement of the recipe (operator said: 'I just wanted as a function that we call manually when needed').
No Playwright removal from v1/parent repo (out of scope; v1 keeps working as-is until archived separately).
No MCP server wiring into Hermes (ad-hoc CLI invocation is sufficient; MCP wiring is a separate decision).
No migration of `infra/camera_creds.py` (the v2 wrapper reads creds at registration time only; the module stays for RTSP-URL validation used by listener).
No new subcommand surface added beyond what reolink-cli 0.19.0 ships — wrapper is a 1:1 typed facade, not a feature layer.
No web dashboard exposure (`reolink-cli gateway` already ships a :9000 dashboard; that's a Reolink concern, not a v2 concern).
No multi-camera batch API (one call per camera is fine; loops live in caller code).
No retry / reconnect logic in the wrapper itself (reolink-cli already handles this; wrapper trusts the binary).
No JSON-schema validation of reolink-cli output (the binary is first-party; trust its JSON shape, document it inline in dataclass field types).
design_principles: Wrapper is a typed facade over a shell subprocess, not a native reolink-cli binding. Reason: reolink-cli IS the canonical Reolink protocol implementation; re-implementing it in Python is duplicate work that drifts from firmware.
Per-camera registration uses `--password-stdin` (or env var `REOLINK_PASSWORD`), never argv. Credentials land in `aliases.toml` once and stay there; no per-call password prompts.
All wrapper methods return dataclasses (`DetectionConfig`, `MotionConfig`, `EncodeConfig`, etc.) with field types matching reolink-cli JSON. No `dict` returns. Caller code is statically checkable.
Errors are typed: `ReolinkCommandError` (non-zero exit), `ReolinkAuthError` (code 401-equivalent), `ReolinkTimeoutError` (subprocess timeout). Caller can branch on these.

Recipe file is TOML not YAML (matches reolink-cli's own config format). Per-camera blocks keyed by the canonical camera slug (FRONT, BACK, OUTSIDE_FRONT_GARAGE, etc.) matching `infra/camera_creds.py`.
Wrapper has zero imports from `listener/`, `infra/frame_capture.py`, `infra/gate.py`, etc. Standalone module. Tested in isolation.
Archive, never delete (AGENTS.md 'no deletions' rule). `scripts/tune_510a_motion_sensitivity.py` moves to `archive/` with a pointer to the new wrapper.

stories.title: infra/reolink.py: typed ReolinkClient facade over reolink-cli subprocess
stories.scope: infra/reolink.py (NEW, ~250 lines): ReolinkClient class with methods `detect_ai_get/set/apply`, `detect_motion_get/set/apply`, `encode_get/set`, `audio_get/set`, `light_get/set`, `image_get/set`, `privacy_get/list/set/delete`, `ptz_*`, `users_list/add/remove/change_password`, `osd_get/set`, `record_get/set`, `events_recent`, `events_stream`, `vod_search`, `vod_download`, `snapshot`, `info`, `capabilities`, `ping`, `device_list`, `login`, `system_reboot`. Dataclasses: DetectionConfig, MotionConfig, EncodeConfig, AudioConfig, LightConfig, ImageConfig, PrivacyMask, UserEntry, OsdConfig, RecordSchedule, EventEntry. Errors: ReolinkCommandError, ReolinkAuthError, ReolinkTimeoutError. Plus __init__.py re-export + tests/test_reolink.py (NEW, ~150 lines, mock subprocess).
acceptance_criteria: ReolinkClient.__init__ accepts optional gateway_addr, binary_path, timeout_sec (env overrides: FARM_REOLINK_GATEWAY_ADDR, FARM_REOLINK_CLI_BIN, FARM_REOLINK_TIMEOUT_SEC).
Every method that hits the camera accepts camera= (alias) OR host= (direct IP). Alias preferred.
All return types are dataclasses with documented fields. No `dict` return types in the public API.
Errors: non-zero exit raises ReolinkCommandError(exit_code, stdout, stderr, command). Timeout raises ReolinkTimeoutError(seconds). Auth failure (matched by stderr pattern) raises ReolinkAuthError.
Tests mock subprocess.run and assert (a) command args, (b) JSON-parsed dataclass output, (c) error mapping, (d) timeout path.
No listener/, infra/frame_capture.py, infra/gate.py imports. Standalone module.
ruff check infra/reolink.py reports zero errors.

stories.title: Register 6 cameras as reolink-cli aliases + config/camera_recipes.toml + apply_recipe/verify_recipe
stories.scope: scripts/register_cameras.py (NEW, ~80 lines): idempotent `device add` for each of FRONT/BACK/OUTSIDE_FRONT_GARAGE/OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR/OUTSIDE_FRONT_POWER/OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR using HTTP_USER/HTTP_PASS from camera-creds.env (password via stdin, never argv). Plus infra/reolink.py: add `apply_recipe(recipe_path, camera=None)` and `verify_recipe(recipe_path, camera=None)` (None=all). Plus config/camera_recipes.toml (NEW): declarative per-camera subcommand configs (e.g. detect_ai.person.stay_time = 2). Plus tests/test_recipe.py (NEW, ~100 lines): round-trip apply+verify against mock CLI.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/register_cameras.py runs cleanly: `python scripts/register_cameras.py` registers all 6 cameras, exits 0. `reolink-cli device list` shows all 6 entries.
No password appears in argv. Verified by grep on argv list (test asserts no '--password X' or trailing position-arg).
Re-registering an existing alias is idempotent (no error, no duplicate entry).
config/camera_recipes.toml follows this shape: [detect_ai.person.FRONT] stay_time = 2 sensitivity = 50; same for vehicle + dog_cat; same per camera. Comment header documents the recipe scope.

apply_recipe(recipe_path, camera=None) loops over all cameras in recipe, calls `detect ai apply` with --stay-time/--sensitivity, asserts verify_recipe returns match=True. Returns per-camera (camera, ok, diff) report.
verify_recipe(recipe_path, camera=None) reads each camera's live state, diffs against recipe, returns per-camera (camera, match, diffs) report. Match=True means all fields equal.
Test asserts apply then verify returns match=True for all 6 cameras using mock CLI.

stories.title: End-to-end live verify: apply + verify recipe against the actual fleet, capture JSON evidence
stories.scope: scripts/verify_recipe_live.py (NEW, ~60 lines): runs `infra.reolink.apply_recipe('config/camera_recipes.toml')` against the live 6 cameras (operator-supplied creds via camera-creds.env), then `verify_recipe()`. Writes evidence JSON to `docs/PHASE-V2-065-verification.json` with per-camera (before, after, match, diffs). Plus docs/PHASE-V2-065-verification.json (NEW, committed artifact).
acceptance_criteria: Script runs against live fleet. Exit 0 = all cameras match recipe. Exit 1 = mismatch with full diff in evidence JSON.
Evidence JSON committed to repo as durable proof: `docs/PHASE-V2-065-verification.json`.
Evidence JSON contains: per-camera {camera, ip, model, before: {detect_ai: {person, vehicle, dog_cat}}, after: {...}, match: bool, diffs: {field: [before, after]}}.
No secrets in evidence JSON (verified by grep; redact if any leak).
Can be re-run any time: `python scripts/verify_recipe_live.py` to confirm fleet still matches recipe.
Output printed to stdout is concise: one line per camera, plus summary (X/6 match).
